prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 220, Part A: stellar rotation and flares (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before js/kernels/activity/, the oracle script, the validator, any pack, panel or lesson of Prompt 220 existed, and before any output of the kernel or the oracle was inspected. Of the two authentic light curves only the file headers were read (cadence, number of rows, sector), to know that the files are what the coordinator said; no period, amplitude or flare list was computed from them.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured is NOT RUN and says why.

seeds.stream: injection (noise draws use stream 'noise'), forked by the check id and the draw index

scope.built: a spotted rotating sphere (circular spots of stated angular radius and contrast, quadratic limb darkening, one rotation axis inclination, a rigid rotation or a stated one-parameter differential rotation, no spot evolution); the rotation period from the repository's existing Lomb-Scargle periodogram (js/kernels/variables/period.js, read unchanged) with a false-alarm probability, a K-harmonic refinement, a profile interval widened by the residual's lag-1 correlation, and the factor-two alias of the peak always reported as a candidate; flare detection by the form of the Chang et al. (2015) criteria after a stated detrend; the equivalent duration in the band with its uncertainty; the flare-frequency distribution in equivalent duration with an exact maximum-likelihood power-law slope; the Davenport et al. (2014) flare template as the seeded injection shape.
scope.notBuilt: any age (gyrochronology) or bolometric flare energy (Part B, gated; nothing in Part A converts an equivalent duration to an energy); spot evolution; spot maps or inversion; faculae; the star's rotation from the light curve as an inference of latitude; a flare classifier; 20-second cadence; the frame branch (Prompt 185 is not on the base).

contract.spotModel: a spot is (lat deg, lon0 deg, radius deg, contrast c) with c the spot's intensity over the photosphere's at the same mu (0 black, 1 invisible); the star has quadratic limb darkening I(mu) = 1 - u1 (1 - mu) - u2 (1 - mu)^2, mu the cosine of the angle to the line of sight, and a rotation axis at inclination inc deg to the line of sight; the observer's direction in the star's frame is (sin inc, 0, cos inc), the spin axis is z, a spot at latitude lat and longitude lam is at (cos lat cos lam, cos lat sin lam, sin lat) with lam = lon0 + 360 (t - t0) / P_lat, and cos gamma = sin inc cos lat cos lam + cos inc sin lat; the normalised flux is 1 - sum_j (1 - c_j) D(gamma_j, rho_j) / [pi (1 - u1/3 - u2/6)] where D is the integral of I(mu) mu over the visible part of the spot's disc; differential rotation is P_lat = P_eq / (1 - k sin^2 lat)
contract.flareTemplate: Davenport et al. (2014), Eqs. 1 and 4, with t in units of t_1/2 (the full width at half maximum of the flare): rise (-1 <= t <= 0) F = 1 + 1.941 t - 0.175 t^2 - 2.246 t^3 - 1.125 t^4; decay (t > 0) F = 0.6890 exp(-1.600 t) + 0.3030 exp(-0.2783 t); the flux excess is amp times F, amp in units of the quiescent flux; the analytic integral over t is 0.307667 + 1.519379 = 1.827046 in units of amp t_1/2, so ED = 1.827046 amp t_1/2
contract.flareRule: the form of Chang et al. (2015): a point is a candidate when (f - q) / sigma >= N1 and (f - q - err) / sigma >= N2 and at least N3 consecutive points qualify; the values N1 = 3, N2 = 2, N3 = 3 are this contract's choice (the default values of the AltaiPony implementation as the author recalls them, not a citation), sigma is the robust scatter (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation) of the detrended residuals, q the quiescent model (a harmonic series at the rotation period fitted with upward clipping, then a running median of 0.25 d, three clipped passes), the flare runs from the first qualifying point back while the excess stays above 1 sigma, to the first point after the peak where it falls below 1 sigma; the equivalent duration is the trapezoidal integral of (f - q) / q over that window

flareRuleDetail.quiescent: three passes; each pass fits a K = 3 harmonic series at the given rotation period by least squares to the unmasked points (no harmonic term when no period is given), takes the residual r = f - h, takes at each point the median of r over the unmasked points whose times lie within +-0.125 d (window 0.25 d) of it, sets q = h + that median, the resid = f - q, sigma = 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of resid over the unmasked points, and masks every point whose resid exceeds 2.5 sigma, extended from it both ways while resid stays at or above 1 sigma (AM2), together with the 2 points on either side; the quiescent model is the last pass
flareRuleDetail.candidates: point i is a candidate when resid_i / sigma >= 3 and (resid_i - err_i) / sigma >= 2, err_i the point error; a run is at least 3 candidates that are consecutive in index with each gap under 1.5 times the median cadence
flareRuleDetail.window: the window starts at the run start and extends backward, and extends forward from the run end, until three consecutive points lie below 1 sigma (AM2; the first version ended at the first such point), its first and last points being the outermost at or above 1 sigma; windows that overlap or touch (gap under 1.5 cadences) are merged; the peak is the largest resid in the window
flareRuleDetail.ed: ED = sum over adjacent window points of 0.5 (g_i + g_{i+1}) (t_{i+1} - t_i) with g = (f - q) / q, over the points of the window, in days times 86400 for seconds; sigma_ED^2 = sum_i (w_i err_i / q_i)^2 + (T_win 1.2533 sigma / (q sqrt(N_w)))^2 with w_i the trapezoid weight in the same unit, T_win the window length and N_w the number of points in the median window (kernel only: the oracle compares times and EDs)
flareRuleDetail.matching: two flares match when their peak times differ by at most 3 cadences
flareRuleDetail.secondStage: after the windows are fixed, the quiescent model is recomputed with a single pass whose starting mask is every point within [window start - ceil(length / 2), window end + 2 length] of any window (length = points in the window), the harmonic series being refitted to the unmasked points and the running median taken over them; the residual, the amplitude and the equivalent duration are then measured against that model over the same windows

authenticPreparation.file: SPOC light-curve FITS, LIGHTCURVE extension: TIME, PDCSAP_FLUX, PDCSAP_FLUX_ERR, QUALITY; kept where QUALITY == 0 and time, flux and error are finite; flux and error divided by the median flux of the kept cadences
authenticPreparation.flares: the 2-minute kept cadences, no binning, flare rule as above with the rotation period of the same star from the rotation search
authenticPreparation.rotation: bins of 30 minutes counted from the first kept time (bin k holds the cadences with floor((t - t_first) / 30 min) = k; a bin with fewer than 8 cadences is dropped; the bin time and flux are the means), search range 0.5 to 13 d (AU Mic) and 0.5 to 13 d (EK Dra), 8 times oversampled, the periodogram of js/kernels/variables/period.js
authenticPreparation.pack: the repository packs carry flux in steps of 100 ppm (binned-relative-flux/2) and the error in steps of errStepPpm, so the kernel reads quantised values; the oracle reads the FITS at full precision and the two are compared with the tolerances above

checks.what: a spot of radius rho at the disc centre (gamma = 0) against the closed form D = 2 pi integral_{cos rho}^{1} I(m) m dm, for rho in {5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 85} deg and (u1, u2) in {(0,0), (0.4,0.22), (0.7,0.1)}
a spot of radius 90 deg at gamma = 0 covers the visible hemisphere: the normalised flux equals the contrast c exactly for c in {0, 0.3, 0.8} at both limb-darkening settings

a spot wholly behind the limb (gamma > 90 deg + rho) changes the flux by exactly zero, and the deficit is continuous through the limb: for rho = 15 deg the largest change of D between gamma steps of 0.01 deg over [60, 120] deg stays under 2e-4 of the central-disc deficit of the same spot
a rigidly rotating star is periodic: |F(t + P) - F(t)| and the mirror symmetry |F(t) - F(P - t)| for one equatorial spot at inc = 90 deg, lon0 = 0, over 200 times
two equal spots 180 deg apart on the equator at inc = 90 deg: |F(t + P/2) - F(t)| over 200 times, and the Lomb-Scargle peak of 400 noiseless samples over 8 periods lies at P/2 within 0.5 per cent
differential rotation: one spot at latitude 50 deg with k = 0.2 and P_eq = 3 d is exactly periodic with P_lat = P_eq / (1 - k sin^2 50 deg): |F(t + P_lat) - F(t)| over 200 times

the flare template's integral: 1.827046 amp t_1/2 against numerical quadrature of the template (relative), and the exposure-integrated 2-minute samples (30 sub-samples a cadence) of a flare with t_1/2 = 10, 30 and 90 min summed times the cadence over amp t_1/2 (ED conserved by integration over the exposure)

the equivalent duration of a boxcar excess h over a width w on a flat baseline (finely sampled, the baseline given) is h w / q within one sample's worth: |ED - h w / q| / (h w / q), h = 0.02 q, w = 20 min, 0.5-min sampling

the maximum-likelihood power-law slope alpha-hat = 1 + n / sum ln(x / x_min) for the list {1, 2, 4} with x_min = 1 (alpha-hat = 1 + 3 / ln 8 = 2.4427) and its exact interval from 2 (alpha - 1) S ~ chi-square with 2n degrees of freedom, S = sum ln(x / x_min): the interval for {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64} against the chi-square quantiles of 14 degrees of freedom (2.5 and 97.5 per cent: 5.629 and 26.119), alpha-hat = 1 + 7 / (21 ln 2)

the kernel's spotted flux against an independent brute-force sky-plane integral (tools/stellar-activity-oracle/oracle.py: 4000 x 4000 pixels over the disc, exact mu, the spot's membership by angular distance, no analytic integral, no quadrature in common) at the 24 configurations listed under oracle.spotConfigs, flux deficit compared

the period search against Astropy's LombScargle (standard normalisation, fit_mean true, center_data true) and numpy on three deterministic light curves written out under oracle.curves: the peak period (relative) and the power at 5 pinned trial periods (absolute)

the flare finder against an independent implementation of the contract's rule (scipy.signal.medfilt and numpy, written from the rule text and not from the kernel) on the seeded synthetic light curve oracle.flareCurve (written out below, 20 injected flares): matched flares (peak times within 3 cadences) as a fraction of each list, and the median relative difference of the matched equivalent durations

the rotation period of the same spotted curves against the oracle's Lomb-Scargle peak refined on a 5000-point grid: the rotation_period primary candidate (or the first candidate when the verdict is a pair) in relative difference; also the two authentic curves of E1 and E3 (the oracle reads the FITS, the kernel the pack), same bound

ensemble of 200 seeded spotted stars (P_eq uniform 0.8 to 12 d, baseline 27 d, 30-minute cadence, noise sigma 1e-3 or 3e-3 by draw parity, inc uniform 50 to 90 deg, u = (0.4, 0.22), one or two spots by draw parity, radii 6 to 15 deg, latitudes within +-60 deg, contrast 0.6, two-spot longitude separation 60 to 120 deg so that the factor-two alias is not the truth): the stated 95 per cent interval of the primary period contains the true P_eq

ensemble of 300 template flares injected on a white-noise baseline (2-minute cadence, sigma 1e-3, amp uniform 12 to 40 sigma, t_1/2 uniform 8 to 40 min, 1 to 3 per curve) and detected with the contract's rule: the stated 95 per cent interval (1.96 sigma_ED) of each matched detected flare contains the injected ED
500 seeded draws of n = 50 equivalent durations from a power law with alpha = 1.8 above x_min = 1: the exact 95 per cent interval contains alpha

injection-recovery on a white-noise baseline (2-minute cadence, sigma 1e-3, 200 injections per cell, a flare counted as recovered when a detected peak lies within 3 cadences): completeness by amp/sigma in {5, 8, 12, 20} and t_1/2 in {4, 10, 30} min is printed for every cell; the stated completeness is graded where the rule can reach it: amp >= 12 sigma and t_1/2 >= 10 min, and amp >= 8 sigma and t_1/2 >= 30 min; the false-positive rate is graded on 40 pure-noise curves of 3000 points
200 seeded white-noise light curves (400 points over 27 d, sigma 1e-3): the verdict is 'no-signal' (false-alarm probability above 0.01 for the best peak) for at least this fraction
a clean single-spot light curve whose period 12 d exceeds half the 15 d baseline: the verdict is 'not-constrained' and no period is reported as a number in 100 per cent of 50 draws

two equal spots 180 deg apart (equator, inc 90 deg, radius 12 deg, noise 1e-3, P_eq 2 to 9 d, 27 d baseline), 100 draws: the Lomb-Scargle peak is near P/2, the reported verdict is the pair ('period-with-alias' with the factor-two alias listed, never a bare single period), and a listed candidate is within 1 per cent of the true P_eq

two spots 180 deg apart with radii 16 and 9 deg (same setting): the odd and even dips differ, the test of the factor-two alias rejects the peak period as the rotation period, and the primary candidate is within 1 per cent of the true P_eq with the half period listed as excluded

100 draws of a single spot whose contrast evolves (contrast rising linearly from 0.55 to 0.95 across the run, a misspecified rigid model): the interval is widened by the residual correlation, the median widening factor is at least this, and on 100 stationary draws of the same star the 95th percentile of the widening factor stays below the second limit

50 spotted stars with no flares (P_eq 0.6 to 3 d, one spot, spot amplitude 3 to 6 per cent, noise 1e-3, 2-minute cadence over 8 d): the finder, run with the rotation period from the kernel's own search, returns no flare in at least this fraction of the curves

AU Mic, TESS sector 1, SPOC 2-minute PDCSAP light curve (file and SHA-256 in D-R10-220-01; the repository's FITS reader), quality-flagged points removed, 30-minute bins, the kernel's rotation period over 0.5 to 13 d: Gilbert et al. (2022, AJ 163, 147; arXiv:2109.03924) report P = 4.85 +- 0.03 d from all TESS sectors (the older literature value they quote is 4.865 d, Torres et al. 1972). Contract: the kernel's primary period lies within 0.03 d of 4.85 d; the factor-two alias (9.7 d) is among the candidates and is not the primary; the verdict is not 'no-signal'

AU Mic sector 1 flares: Gilbert et al. (2022) find 48 flares in 25.07 d at 2-minute cadence (1.855 per day) with their own pipeline and thresholds. Contract (applicability, not a reproduction: another detector and another threshold): the contract's rule returns a rate within the band, and the oracle's independent implementation of the same rule on the same light curve agrees with the kernel as in B3 on the real data

EK Draconis (a young Sun-like star), TESS sector 16, SPOC 2-minute PDCSAP (file and SHA-256 in D-R10-220-01): the literature gives about 2.77 d (Audard et al. 1999; Ayres 2015; Namekata et al. 2022) and about 2.6 d (Gorgei et al. 2026) and attributes the difference to differential rotation; no single published period with an uncertainty for this sector is claimed. Contract: the kernel's primary period lies in [2.50, 2.90] d, the span of the cited values with 0.1 d of margin, and the factor-two alias is among the candidates and not the primary

the AU Mic sector-1 flare-frequency distribution of the contract's detections above the completeness limit read off C4 (the smallest equivalent duration at which the graded cells are complete, rounded up to the next table cell): the maximum-likelihood slope alpha lies in [1.4, 2.6], the range of published flare-frequency slopes of active M dwarfs; the interval is printed (an applicability check: no published slope for this sector is claimed)
the kernel's rotation period against the oracle's independent K = 4 harmonic-series period (added by AM3): the three curves, and the two authentic series in E1 and E3

two spots 180 deg apart with radii 12 and 10.5 deg (added by AM4; same setting as D4, 100 draws): the peak is at half the period, the factor-two test rejects it, the primary candidate is within 1 per cent of the true P_eq and the half period is listed as excluded

spotConfigs.note: 24 configurations, each [gamma deg, rho deg, u1, u2, contrast]: five gammas by three radii at (0.4, 0.22) and contrast 0.5; six at gamma 60, rho 30 with other limb darkening and contrast; three behind-the-limb-centre spots

curves.note: three deterministic noiseless spotted curves, 600 samples uniform over 24 d (t = 24 i / 600), u = (0.4, 0.22), inc 70 deg, contrast 0.6: (1) P 4.2 d, one spot lat 20 lon0 30 radius 12; (2) P 2.9 d, two spots (lat 25, lon0 0, radius 10) and (lat -30, lon0 110, radius 8); (3) P 7.5 d, one spot lat 45 lon0 200 radius 15 with k = 0.15. Trial periods for the power: 1.5, 2.9, 4.2, 5.0 and 7.5 d.

flareCurve.note: 2-minute cadence, 3000 points from t = 0, baseline 1 + 0.02 sin(2 pi t / 1.7 d), Gaussian noise sigma 1e-3 (numpy default_rng(220)), twenty flares with t_peak = (4 + 4.5 k) hours after the start for k = 0..19 plus 0.37 h times (k mod 3), amp = 0.006 + 0.004 (k mod 5), t_1/2 = (8 + 3 (k mod 4)) minutes, the template of the contract, exposure-integrated over 5 sub-samples

amendments.when: before the oracle was run and before any kernel existed; no bound moved
amendments.what: The flare rule and the authentic preparation are written out so that the oracle and the kernel implement the same rule independently.

amendments.when: after the first run of C2 (coverage 0.0465 of 301 injected flares, detected fraction 1.0) and B3 (all matched); no bound moved
amendments.what: The quiescent model masked only the points above 2.5 sigma and two on either side, so a flare's wings (above 1 sigma and below 2.5 sigma) lifted the running median and took about a third of the flare's own light out of its equivalent duration, in the kernel and in the oracle alike (which is why B3 agreed). The rule now extends each seed point both ways while the excess stays at or above 1 sigma before the 2-point dilation. The oracle was changed in the same way and re-run; every other oracle result is unchanged. C2's bound (coverage 0.90) is the original. Second change of AM2, found in the same investigation: the window ended at the first point below 1 sigma, so one noise dip in a flare's 2 sigma tail ended it early (the kernel then returned about two thirds of a flare's equivalent duration and split some flares in two). The window now runs on until three consecutive points lie below 1 sigma, at both ends, and the end point is the last point at or above 1 sigma. Kernel and oracle both follow.

amendments.when: after the first run of B4; B4 stays as committed
amendments.what: B4 compares the kernel's refined period (the K-harmonic scatter minimum) with the oracle's Lomb-Scargle sinusoid peak and measured 0.84 per cent against the bound 0.2 per cent on a sheared, non-sinusoidal curve (the kernel recovers the true period of each synthetic curve to 1e-4; the sinusoid peak does not): B4 is left failing and labelled in failed-legs.json. A new leg B5 is added with the same bound 2e-3: the oracle's independent K = 4 harmonic-series period (scipy bounded minimisation of the least-squares scatter, no Gravitas code) against the kernel's, on the three curves and the two authentic series. B5 is an addition; it does not replace B4.

amendments.when: after the first run of D4; D4 stays as committed
amendments.what: D4 (radii 16 and 9 deg) measured primaryOk 100 of 100 but excluded 0 of 100: with spots of that unequal size the Lomb-Scargle peak is the rotation period itself, not the half period, so the factor-two test is never asked and the verdict is 'period-with-alias' with the true period as primary (correct, and not what D4's text premised). D4 is left failing and labelled in failed-legs.json. A new leg D4b is added to exercise the 'double-period' verdict where the premise holds: radii 12 and 10.5 deg, every other setting as D4, 100 draws: the peak lies at half the period, the verdict is 'double-period' and the primary candidate is within 1 per cent of the true P_eq, with the half period listed as excluded, in at least 0.95 of the draws.

amendments.when: after the first run of E2 (matched fractions 0.83 and 0.90, median relative ED difference 0.31 against 0.1); no bound moved
amendments.what: AM2 added a second stage to the kernel (the quiescent model recomputed once, with every detected window extended before by half its length and after by twice it masked from the start, the windows themselves unchanged) that the oracle did not have, so on AU Mic's long flares the two lists measured different excesses. The second stage is part of the rule text now (contract.flareRuleDetail.secondStage) and the oracle implements it from that text; its results were re-pinned. B3 (synthetic, matched 1.0, median 0.039) was unaffected by the change in kind.
